description.value: A weekend-only Hong Kong-inspired gluten-free cafe occupying a family space in Vancouver's historic Chinatown corridor that has been in the owners' family for three generations. The kitchen specialises in nostalgic Cantonese comfort food — gluten-free baos, noodles, rice bowls, and soy sauce chicken — alongside Hong Kong-style milk teas, seasonal cocktails, and local craft beer. Cyclists with dietary restrictions will find a rare dedicated gluten-free kitchen with clear vegan and nut-free options on offer.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is accessible and serves as primary evidence. The website consistently lists the address as '227 Main St.' across every page, while the OSM record states '277 Main Street' — a clear discrepancy flagged in concerns and resolved in favour of the website. The website confirms takeout/pickup ('Pre-Order For Pick-Up & Delivery Now!'), a dedicated gluten-free kitchen with explicit vegan options and vegetarian menu items marked (v), and OSM tags confirm customer-accessible washrooms (toilets=yes, toilets:access=customers) with no website contradiction. No bike parking, water refill, Wi-Fi, or charging amenities are mentioned on the website; OSM internet_access=no is not treated as authoritative per rules, so Wi-Fi remains null.
concerns: Address discrepancy: OSM records '277 Main Street' but the business website consistently displays '227 Main St.' on every page — the civic address should be verified before publishing; this listing uses the website value of 227 Main St.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, active, publicly accessible restaurant with a live website, current menu, and confirmed operating hours. Clearly open to the public and useful to touring cyclists.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Menu disclaimer: 'We are a dedicated gluten free cafe. We also offer vegan and nut free options.' Multiple menu items marked (v) for vegetarian
